entities.name: George Percy
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
George Percy (1580–1632) was an English aristocrat, explorer, and colonial administrator whose pivotal, albeit often overlooked, role in the nascent Jamestown settlement proved critical to the survival of England's first permanent New World colony. As the youngest son of Henry Percy, 8th Earl of Northumberland, he leveraged his noble connections for a career in exploration and governance, chronicling some of the earliest and most challenging years of English engagement with North America during the Early Modern Era. His detailed written accounts remain indispensable primary sources for understanding the hardships, political machinations, and environmental realities faced by the initial English colonists in Virginia.

Percy's career began with military service in the Low Countries, followed by a voyage to Guiana in 1606. He was among the 104 original colonists who landed at Jamestown in May 1607, playing an active role in the settlement's establishment and early defense. He served on the colony's council and, crucially, as Deputy Governor from September 1609 to May 1610, during the harrowing "Starving Time." Despite his personal suffering and the immense death toll, Percy maintained order and leadership, documenting the period's extreme famine, disease, and conflict with the Powhatan Confederacy in his 'A Trewe Relacyon' and 'Observations Gathered Out of a Discourse of the Plantation of the Southern Colony in Virginia by the English.' He returned to England in 1612, later serving again in military capacities.
